steps.prompt: Hold Left Shift with your pinky, then tap a right-hand letter.
steps.text: Hi Jo Ki Lo Up In On My No Hu

steps.prompt: Opposite hands: left shift, right letter.
steps.text: Harry Jill Kim Lily Uma Nina Oscar Milo

steps.prompt: Capital letters start names.
steps.text: Nina met Oscar and Jill likes Kim Milo and Uma ran up

steps.prompt: Hold Right Shift, then tap a left-hand letter.
steps.text: As Be Cat Dog Ever Fox Go Red Tea Van

steps.prompt: Opposite hands: right shift, left letter.
steps.text: Amy Ben Cara Dan Finn Gus Rex Tess Walt

steps.prompt: Capitalize every word.
steps.text: A Big Red Fox The Grey Cat We Are Done Now

steps.prompt: Right ring taps the period, right middle taps the comma.
steps.text: l. k, l. k, end. yes, no, ok.

steps.prompt: Now sentences can stop and pause.
steps.text: The cat sat. The dog ran, and she won. We ate, then we slept.

steps.prompt: Right pinky taps ' and (with shift) the ? key.
steps.text: it's I'm can't who? why? how?

steps.prompt: Ask a question, use a contraction.
steps.text: Who is it? It's Max. Can't you see? I'm sure it's fine.

steps.prompt: ! is Shift and 1. The hyphen joins words.
steps.text: Wow! Go! Stop! well-made top-notch ten-year-old

steps.prompt: Add some excitement.
steps.text: Watch out! That was a well-timed, top-notch move! Great job!

steps.prompt: Reach up to the number row with the left hand.
Mix numbers and letters.

steps.prompt: Reach up with the right hand.
All ten numbers now.
steps.text: j6 k7 l8 90 the year 2026; 100 steps; 7 of 10; 9 to 5

steps.prompt: Type the words you use most, smoothly.
steps.text: the and you that was for are with his they have this from word what some

steps.prompt: Keep a steady rhythm.
steps.text: when your said each which them then many these would write like into time has

steps.prompt: Capitals, spaces and periods together.
steps.text: She opened the door and looked outside. The rain had stopped at last.

steps.prompt: Pause at the commas.
steps.text: After lunch, we walked to the park, fed the ducks, and headed home.

steps.prompt: Your longest type yet. Take your time.
steps.text: A good typist does not look at the keys. She keeps her eyes on the words and lets her fingers find their way home. Speed comes later; first comes a calm, steady hand.
